label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/snapbug.mdl, models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, D, A where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Every side view (front, left, back, right, and the four angled views) shows the same straight-sided cylinder with a flat top and bottom. The outline matches a 55-gallon drum, with two rolling hoops and a rim bevel on the lid, and nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Measured size is 22.6 x 22.6 x 35 units against the brief's 23 across and 34 high, so it is within 3% on each measure, well inside the 15% band.

M3.reason: Parts listed from the brief: drum body, top and bottom lids, rolling hoops, and the hazard stripe. The brief names no further small parts such as bungs or handles. The top and bottom hoops are on every side view (FRONT, LEFT, FRONT-LEFT), and the lid's bevel is in TOP and BELOW. All are present in the right places.

M4.reason: The hazard stripe is yellow and black and the hoops are light steel, as the brief asks. But the brief says rusted, and the body (FRONT, LEFT, BACK, RIGHT) is an even blue-grey steel with almost no rust on it. Brown rust shows only as patches on the hoops, in FRONT at the top hoop and in BACK at the bottom. The body's material does not read as rusted.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe is sharp and in its place, and the hoops carry rust streaks. But the body has little rust, pitting or wear. A vertical texture seam runs down the centre of the FRONT view, through the stripe and both hoops, where the pattern breaks.

M6.reason: In the four-way line-up (lineup.png, asset at B) the judges picked a Valve original as the one not made by Valve in all four readings, so the asset was never picked. It passes as one of the game's props at this scale. Capped at 2 by the rubric.

M7.reason: The drum stands upright on a flat base (BELOW view shows a closed bottom), and the lid is on top. The brief gives no front, so the orientation is the natural upright one.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. At 96 triangles it is under the Half-Life median of 99 for props of its kind, far under twice that. Both lids are closed in BELOW and TOP, and no face is open or inside out in any view.
